_source.note: The README has nine top-level sections. Everything below is from `## Features` only; that section has no sub-headings, so every entry carries the same section name.

counting_rule.rule: One feature = one paragraph inside `## Features` that opens with a bold lead, i.e. a line matching /^\*\*/. The bold lead is the feature name; the sentence after it is the description.
counting_rule.shell_equivalent: sed -n '/^## Features/,/^## Security notes/p' README.md | grep -c '^\*\*'
caveats: This is the DOCUMENTED count, not the built count. The README has not changed since 13 Sep (byte-identical), while four user-facing features landed 14–15 Sep: phone sound routing (computer / phone / both), the Claude-tab terminal fixes, the School pane filling its pane, and the phone workspace keeping exactly one phone tab. None of those four are in the 67.

The rule matters: the whole README carries 70 bold-lead paragraphs, and three of them sit outside `## Features`, in sections that use the same style for things that are not features. Counting only inside `## Features` is what gives 67.
A few paragraphs open with more than one bold run — e.g. "**Trading** … and **Phone** …" — so `name` is the FIRST bold run only, and `lead_raw` carries the whole opening line as the README writes it.
